blocks.text: GOVERNOR OF JUDAH · EXILE & RETURN
Nehemiah. Twelve years governor; the wall rebuilt in fifty-two days.
GOVERNEDi
12 years c. 445–433 BC (dates vary)
SEAT
Jerusalem
HOUSE

SCRIPTURE SAYS
“The former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people… but so did not I, because of…”
PROPHETS
Shemaiah son of Delaiah · Noadiah
PERSIA: 9 RULERS CYRUS → NEHEMIAH
AUTHORITY
Under whose authority
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"The former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people… but so did not I, because of the fear of God." Nehemiah 5:15
"Think upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people." Nehemiah 5:19
"Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in." Nehemiah 6:11
"These were in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua… and in the days of Nehemiah the governor, and of Ezra the priest, the scribe." Nehemiah 12:26
His last words in the book: "Remember me, O my God, for good." Nehemiah 13:31

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
From Artaxerxes' twentieth year to his thirty-second: 12 years (Neh 5:14).
IF ARTAXERXES I: 445–433 BC (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)
Artaxerxes I's twentieth year began in spring 445 and his thirty-second in spring 433.
Ryle: the twentieth year is 445 BC; Cowley, from the Elephantine letter, concludes that the thirty-second year was 433 BC.
Artaxerxes I
H. E. Ryle (1893); R. Dick Wilson (1915); A. Cowley (1923)

Sanballat's sons and the high priest Johanan appear in an Elephantine letter of 408 BC, which fits Sanballat as Nehemiah's opponent about 445 and makes Nehemiah's king Artaxerxes I, not II. Nehemiah 2:10 Nehemiah 12:22 [34][17][6]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long his second stay lasted, or when and where he died.
Scripture does not name the governors between Zerubbabel and Nehemiah; he speaks only of "the former governors that had been before me" (Neh 5:15).
Nehemiah 1:1 dates the news to Chisleu "in the twentieth year" and 2:1 his audience to Nisan of Artaxerxes' twentieth year; Scripture does not explain how the two months fall in one year.
Scripture calls Sanballat only "the Horonite"; the title "governor of Samaria" comes from the Elephantine letter.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textNehemiah son of Hachaliah is a different man from the Nehemiah who came up with Zerubbabel and from Nehemiah son of Azbuk. Nehemiah 1:1 Ezra 2:2 Nehemiah 3:16
From the textHe calls himself governor, and the book calls him "Nehemiah the governor" and "Nehemiah, which is the Tirshatha". Nehemiah 5:14 Nehemiah 12:26 Nehemiah 8:9 Nehemiah 10:1
Scholars' view"Tirshatha" is a Persian-era title; R. Dick Wilson (1915) notes it stands beside pechah, "governor", for the same men.[16]
